articles.title_orig: Trump says Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets
articles.title_zh: Trump says Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets
articles.content_orig:
A new pact that calls for Russia to boost the U.S. supply of diesel over the next few months is unlikely to make a dent in painfully high prices at the pump or elsewhere, energy policy experts say.
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he had struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to immediately supply the U.S. more than 300,000 tons of diesel. That would be followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November, then 4 million more tons at some point after that.
The deal marks a stark reversal of policy by the U.S., which from the start of Russia's war with Ukraine had banned imports of Russian oil, and comes at a time when the U.S. economy and consumers are being squeezed by a global rise in oil prices due to the eight-month-long U.S. war with Iran .
The price of diesel has shattered records in recent weeks, ratcheting up inflation for a broad swath of consumer goods.
The national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. hit a record high of $6.53 on Sept. 22, according to motor club AAA. It averaged nearly $6.28 a gallon on Friday, up from almost $3.68 this time last year. Diesel prices have hit records in Europe, too.
Higher diesel prices mean more expensive transportation for a long list of everyday goods. That's because diesel is used for many freight and delivery networks. And some businesses have already passed along steeper costs to consumers in the form of added fees on online orders and packages in the mail .
Shoppers may feel more and more sticker shock, particularly in the grocery aisle. Perishable foods, like meat and produce, face one of the most immediate strains of expensive diesel because they need to be hauled in and restocked frequently — or may be harvested using farm equipment powered by the fuel.
That's turned up the heat on Trump and the Republican Party to address surging prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections . The president's approval ratings on the economy have hit a new low, according to an AP-NORC poll released last week, as the Iran war and his trade battles have increased U.S. prices for oil and other goods.
Energy policy experts on Friday expressed doubts that a boost in diesel supply from Russia will have a significant impact on oil prices, whether in the U.S. or globally.
"It's kind of shuffling deck chairs on the Titanic," said Michael Lynch, distinguished fellow at Energy Policy Research Foundation, a nonpartisan research institution focused on energy and economics.
"If we get diesel from Russia, basically it means that their existing customers are not going to get it and they'll have to go somewhere else, and that will keep the price basically where it is now," Lynch said.
And while the White House may be counting on this move to give some relief at the pump for U.S. truckers, ranchers and farmers who have been hit hard by rising diesel prices, that's not a given.
"The best you could hope for is a tiny dip in prices locally in places like the New York-New Jersey area, Philadelphia maybe," Lynch said. "It just means that the oil is just going to be shuffled around and it's not really going to change the price globally or across the U.S."
If Russia, which in July moved to ban diesel exports due to Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries, now believes it is able to resume exports of diesel, then that will help stabilize global diesel prices, said Daniel Sternoff, senior fellow at the Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy.
However, prices are likely to remain elevated overall because a lot of refining capacity in the Middle East isn't available to the world market due to the disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz from the ongoing U.S.-Iran war.
"Refined products like diesel are still barely half of prewar levels," Sternoff said. "So, even if there were to be some follow-through from the Russians to put a little extra diesel into the world markets, it might take the edge off of prices, but it will not substantially lower them."
While the deal between Trump and Putin probably won't have much of an impact on prices for diesel consumers in the U.S., it will benefit Russia, said Clayton Seigle, an energy strategist and expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
That's because Russia is trying to offload its summer-grade diesel for the heavier winter and arctic grades that they will need in the coming months, Seigle noted.
"I don't think it'll be enough to materially lower prices in the United States or Europe, but it does certainly let Moscow off the hook in terms of revenue squeeze," he said.

articles.title_orig: iPhone Duo buyers to get a special surprise at U.S. Apple Stores, Gurman says
articles.title_zh: iPhone Duo buyers to get a special surprise at U.S. Apple Stores, Gurman says
articles.content_orig:
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, iPhone Duo buyers who purchase their device at an Apple Store in the US will be treated to a nice little surprise when they turn it on for the first time. Here are the details.
When Apple launches the iPhone Duo on October 23, some customers who purchase the device at an Apple Store in the US will be able to have its initial setup screen personalized with their name.
According to Gurman, “Apple retail stores will have a system to customize the boot of the device,” allowing the iPhone Duo to display a greeting containing their name when it turns on for the first time. Gurman says the feature will be exclusive to the iPhone Duo, and support both English and Spanish.
Fun little touch for the iPhone Duo launch: Apple retail stores will have a system to customize the boot of the device with the buyer's name so it says "Hello, Mark" (for example) when it turns on for the first time. (US only, Duo only, English and Spanish).
It is not clear how Apple will implement the feature, or whether it will rely on Presto , the system Apple Stores already use to wirelessly update iPhones without removing them from their boxes.
If I were to implement it, I'd have the name associated with the device serial, which they already record when selling the phone. Get the phone to automatically find and connect to the Apple Store Wi-Fi on the first power up and download the name. That's probably why it only works in-store.
First reported by Gurman in 2023, Presto allows Apple retail employees to turn on an iPhone, install software updates, and turn it off again, all while the device remains sealed in its packaging.
Back to the iPhone Duo, it will be available to pre-order starting Friday, October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability beginning October 23.
Apple recently announced that customers will be able to get ready for iPhone Duo pre-orders beginning October 12, and you can read more about that here .

articles.title_orig: Amazon shuffles Alexa leadership following high-end tablet release
articles.title_zh: Amazon shuffles Alexa leadership following high-end tablet release
articles.content_orig:
Amazon on Thursday debuted a set of new, pricier Alexa tablets and said it's ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup, marking a significant shift in the e-commerce juggernaut's devices strategy.
The company unveiled 8-inch, 11-inch and 12-inch models, which start at $230 and run up to $550. All devices are available for preorder on Thursday and will begin shipping Oct. 14.
Amazon has historically sold its devices at or near the cost of manufacturing them, partly to undercut competitors with extremely cheap prices, but also with the goal of promoting its other products and services. It's hoped that for every $80 Echo smart speaker it sells, users will purchase movies, audiobook subscriptions or items from its sprawling webstore, which tend to have higher margins.
The company has recently taken steps to make more money from its devices business under CEO Andy Jassy , who succeeded founder Jeff Bezos in 2021. Last year, it introduced pricier versions of its Echo smart speakers and began charging non-Prime members a subscription for Alexa+ , the souped-up version of its digital assistant.
The $550 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro costs more than double the price of the $155 Fire HD 10, Amazon's base model, and puts it more in line with Apple 's iPad, which runs from $449 to $1,199.
The launch comes as Amazon and other device makers are grappling with a historic surge in memory prices . Amazon in August boosted prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs and other hardware, citing the memory crunch. And earlier this year, Apple raised its prices on MacBooks and iPads, while Nintendo hiked the price of its Switch 2 console.
Amazon denied that rising memory costs played a role in its decision to charge more for the Alexa tablet. But Panos Panay, the company's devices boss, acknowledged that the shortage made it "quite tricky" to build a premium tablet at a reasonable price without making any "trade-offs."
"I think the team did a good job designing without making that trade," Panay told CNBC in an interview. "They gave you the full craftsmanship of a product, but are able to keep it at that price point."
The company said the Alexa tablet's improved speed and performance, artificial intelligence features, and upgraded design warrant a higher price tag and put the devices on par with "the best tablets on the market."
Amazon added a sleeker, sturdier aluminum backing, higher resolution display and faster processors. On the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the highest-end model, it incorporated "Nanomatte" display technology that was developed in partnership with Corning to "dramatically reduce screen glare."
One of the most notable upgrades is that all of the devices run Google 's Android operating system, a major departure from earlier models, which relied on a custom Android version dubbed Fire OS and used Amazon's own app store, limiting the number of apps that were available.
It's also the first time Amazon has attached a set of devices to the Alexa brand, the company's automated assistant first launched in 2014 via the Echo smart speaker. Alexa is front and center in the new tablets, via a "dynamic tab" on the home screen that offers recommendations and lets users quickly pick up where they left off reading or watching a TV show. Users can say "Alexa" or tap the "Ask Alexa" button to ask questions.
The company also introduced a new feature called "On-Screen Intelligence," where users can ask Alexa to look at what's on their screen and make suggestions or take actions.
In a demo, Panay showed how users could watch a TikTok clip of someone cooking on a grill and ask Alexa to shop for a burger press used in the video. Users can also pull up a game schedule and add every date to their calendar, Amazon said.
"She'll do the homework, and if things work out, she's going to bring up a shopping list where I can just hit buy now," Panay said.
Amazon said it will continue to support the Fire lineup for four years after the final shipment and consumers can continue using their devices as they do today, but it is no longer manufacturing new units. The Fire lineup includes a 10-inch and 8-inch model as well as two versions targeted for kids.

articles.title_orig: NASA issues long-awaited call to industry for private space stations
articles.title_zh: NASA issues long-awaited call to industry for private space stations
articles.content_orig:
NASA on Friday released a much-anticipated “request” to the US commercial space industry to develop private space stations that, as early as 2030, will succeed the International Space Station as a place for astronauts to live in low-Earth orbit.
In a cover letter accompanying the 360-page “request for proposals,” NASA stated its plan: “This will ensure NASA has a sustained human presence in LEO for crew members to perform science and exploration.” Several private companies that have worked for years on designing and developing such stations have been keen to learn exactly what capabilities NASA is seeking. These new documents finally provide some answers.
NASA’s solicitation can be found here . Industry responses are due back to NASA on December 8. NASA said it plans to select “two or more” contractors in this phase of the competition, and intends to make a final decision in April.
“We’ve made it clear that NASA will never give up its presence in low Earth orbit,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a statement that accompanied the release of the new documents. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars. Commercial space stations may provide that capability while creating new opportunities for American industry and allowing NASA to concentrate more of our resources on the near-impossible missions ahead.”
Bidders for this funding phase will certainly include Axiom Space, Voyager Space, and Vast Space. Blue Origin won an earlier round of funding from NASA, but questions remain about the company’s commitment to the program. SpaceX appears unlikely to bid, at least for now. Phase 1 winners will be guaranteed at least $100 million.
Future phases of the contract will be worth billions. NASA said Phase 2 of this “Commercial LEO Destinations” competition, kicking off next year, will include funding for development and certification of space stations, and Phase 3 will include the purchase of at least four missions for NASA astronauts to the private space stations.
One of the most closely watched elements of the NASA request was its provisions for crewed transportation to the stations. In earlier discussions with potential space station providers, NASA had indicated it may leave acquiring transportation to the contractors—basically saying it was their responsibility to sell an end-to-end service to the space agency.
This is problematic because SpaceX has said it plans to retire the Crew Dragon spacecraft as soon as possible, and almost certainly when the International Space Station is deorbited in 2030 or 2032. SpaceX, which has the only operational US vehicle for such transportation, has not offered to sell seats to private space station operators. This led NASA, two weeks ago , to provide an additional $359 million to support Boeing’s ongoing efforts to certify its Starliner spacecraft for crewed missions to low-Earth orbit.
But in the new request for proposals (RFP), the space agency goes further in support of would-be space station operators. As part of their bids, contractors do not need to provide proof of a signed contract with Boeing (or another transportation provider), or even a letter of intent. NASA is even offering to “furnish” transportation for the first four NASA service missions to the private stations, likely meaning it will help broker deals between the private companies and Boeing.
Notably, in the new documents, NASA assigns an explicit price to crew and cargo missions. For 2030, it estimates a four-seat crew flight will cost $325 million, and a cargo flight $300 million. In offering to furnish these initial flights, NASA is taking a significant burden off private space station providers, which are already undertaking a challenging task in constructing, testing, and flying orbital space stations.
The potential bidders were still reviewing the lengthy proposal on Friday afternoon, but several offered their initial thoughts on the new NASA documents.
“The release of the RFP is an important milestone,” Marshall Smith, the chief executive of Voyager’s Starlab space station, said. “We appreciate that NASA has incorporated both industry and government feedback. We believe Starlab has the strongest business plan and technical solution to be America’s next space station and we look forward to competing.”
Axiom Space said it also welcomed the release of the final RFP.
“Our team is actively reviewing the RFP now and is energized for the next steps in the process,” an Axiom Space spokesperson said. “With years of experience executing human space flight missions and developing orbital hardware, we are confident the proposal we provide NASA will demonstrate that Axiom Space is the clear choice to meet NASA’s objectives in low-Earth orbit.”
Vast, too, said it was prepared to move forward with the competition.
“Vast looks forward to competing for the opportunity to build the commercial successor to the ISS,” a company spokesperson said. “We’re in final integration with Haven-1 and ready to keep building towards a multi-module station capable of supporting a continuous human presence.”

articles.title_orig: Everything We Expect From Apple’s Surprise Smart Home Event Next Week
articles.title_zh: Everything We Expect From Apple’s Surprise Smart Home Event Next Week
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
We now have confirmation of Apple’s massive ‘Welcome Home” smart home event happening on Tuesday. Invitations went out on Thursday with a distinctive rainbow-colored Apple logo. So many things are expected to be announced, centering on Apple and Siri entering the home tech space in all-new ways. The tech giant’s smart home devices will face serious competition from Amazon , Google and other players.
Over the past few weeks, I’ve been collecting the reports, insider claims and possible leaks to see just what Apple could be announcing. It all points to a major shake-up for home security , smart home devices and how Siri AI can be used . CNET will be there in person to see what Apple has cooked up, but in the meantime, here are the latest rumors.
A representative from Apple didn’t respond to a request for comment.
For more than a year, Apple has been rumored to be readying a Siri-focused smart display hub for the home, sometimes referred to as a HomePad, though we don’t know for sure that’ll be the name. This display would focus heavily on Siri AI and compete with products like Amazon’s Echo Show and the Google Nest Hub line by acting as a HomeKit hub.
Smart displays can add a lot of functionality to smart speakers , if you don’t mind using voice assistants. Rumors suggest the display could swivel and/or be attached to a wall, be at least several inches wide and allow Siri to recognize different people in a conversation. In terms of size, we’ve heard rumors putting it around 6 inches, with the screen attached to a HomePod-like speaker and powered by regular AC power rather than USB-C.
Smart touchscreens are great for getting visual information, watching videos or viewing to-do lists, so a display like this is likely to have a bit of Apple TV and Safari in it, too. While the Apple TV 4K, iPad and current HomePod models can already act as HomeKit hubs, I expect Apple to offer a real UI and UX experience designed for smart displays, making it a stronger argument for having in your home alongside other devices.
Is it likely? I think it’s quite likely, based on how many insider reports have mentioned this smart display, but I don’t think we have a good idea how it will look yet.
Along with a smart display, rumors are flying that Apple will give its HomePod smart speaker line the first major update in years. It’s the ideal time to update the HomePod line, too, although it’s possible some of these reports have confused plans for a smart display with a new smart speaker, both of which could fall under the HomePod label.
If a new HomePod speaker is on the horizon, reports indicate that it would be a new type of HomePod Mini. That’s not surprising — the original HomePod has often been critiqued for being over $300, which is why Apple focused on the less expensive Mini model afterward. One welcome leak I’ve seen is that there will be new colors for the HomePod Mini 2, including green and pink, and a faster S-series chip.
Is it likely? Yes, I’d say this is about as likely as a Siri smart display, if Apple wants to continue developing the HomePod line.
The same reports that say a smart display and new HomePod are on the way also mention Apple is planning to release a new Apple TV model. This model is rumored to have upgraded specs, with a faster N1 processor, 8GB RAM, Wi-Fi 7 and an upgraded Siri remote.
It’s a product line that’s sort of connected to the smart home, especially if Apple is launching a smart display. The company hasn’t released a new set-top box since 2022 , so it’s about time for another. This could also give the Apple TV new hardware for extra Siri AI tricks. There’s also been some speculation that this will be compatible with the new HomePods, allowing you to set up multiple units in a surround sound-style home cinema.
Is it likely? I think it’s less likely than a speaker or display. It’s not quite as much of a smart home gadget, and it seems to have gotten swept into the wide net of rumors, but without as many reports.
Recent rumors says Apple is ready to enter the home security world with its own products. Although we don’t know much, reports from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman say these will be tiny cameras that, interestingly, won’t record any video. No recording means Apple won’t have to worry about cloud storage and may be able to avoid charging extra subscriptions for them.
The cameras are rumored to have some kind of presence-sensing or human-recognizing technology as well as AI video descriptions, suggesting Apple Home will be running analysis on the video even if it won’t record permanently. The phrase “facial recognition” was also mentioned, but this doesn’t seem nearly as likely to me. This may be related to a rumor about Apple’s Ring-like doorbell camera, which may come with Face ID for unlocking a door, but this would likely be separate from the non-recording indoor security cameras.
Is it likely? I’m betting on some kind of home security announcement, and I expect Apple would like to have its own camera line, but I don’t know if this exact product will be released. However, the extra details do lend this rumor legitimacy.
Apple may be partnering with LG for some smart home devices, and there are even reportedly leaked product concept photos circulating on the internet. One of the biggest potential releases is an Apple-friendly thermostat . The photos show a round, Nest-like thermostat dial, and rumors say it will include far-sight presence sensing, a humidity sensor and several temperature calibration options.
2. LG Smart Thermostat •  Settings for Far Sight Display, Humidity Display, Brightness, Language. •  Calibrated Temperature/Temperature Offset options. pic.twitter.com/Q8AAaxy4ey
Alongside the thermostat, the Apple/LG combo is expected to release a sensor that can measure the temperature at specific locations and feed that information back to the thermostat hub. That would be no surprise, because models from Nest, Ecobee and others have similar satellite sensors , although Apple’s may have adhesive strips to attach its version to the wall.
Apple partnered with LG years ago to support Apple-friendly security cameras, but those lines were rarely updated and quickly became obsolete. Maybe Apple is ready to try again with a different approach.
Is it likely? If Apple really is partnering with LG for a new wave of home devices, I think a thermostat is likely. But this is starting to be a lot of products to announce at a single October event that won’t be publicly streamed.
The other big rumor centering around an LG collaboration is an Apple smart lock . While many smart locks work with Apple and Apple Home Keys, the tech giant hasn’t been involved in the development of a smart lock before.
It could have automatic unlocking, tapping your phone to unlock and a variety of keypad management options. That’s not surprising, but the rumored product images show a round, twist-to-unlock, light-up outdoor keypad, and I haven’t seen anything like that before.
If Apple does release a smart lock , Ring will have beaten it to the punch with its own announcement of its first-ever lock , which will include Alexa compatibility and a unique thumbturn that can generate a charge when the battery dies.
EXCLUSIVE 👀 First look at LG’s upcoming smart home lineup: LG Video Doorbell Wired LG Floodlight Cam LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In LG Indoor Cam Plug-In pic.twitter.com/vblGECQLM1
Other rumors and purported product images suggest the LG partnership could also yield a video doorbell, floodlight camera, outdoor camera and indoor camera . These seem to be LG-branded devices, however, and I can’t imagine Apple releasing products that look like this.
Is it likely? Now this is a lot of new gadgets to announce at once. I think a smart lock is about as likely as a smart thermostat; those are both strong field

articles.title_orig: Fired OpenAI employees question the company's commitment to safety
articles.title_zh: Fired OpenAI employees question the company's commitment to safety
articles.content_orig:
Three employees recently fired by OpenAI allege the company punished them for being outspoken about safety. OpenAI disputes the claims and says they were dismissed for mishandling sensitive information. Andrej Ivanov/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Three former OpenAI employees are raising concerns over the circumstances of their dismissals and the company's commitment to safety, amid intense public scrutiny of the artificial intelligence industry's ability to responsibly develop the technology .
The former employees, Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, alleged that OpenAI fired them last week over pretexts and punished them for either being outspoken about safety or working with outside researchers. They also expressed worries the company may walk back a recent safety commitment.
OpenAI has repeatedly denied the allegations. It said the employees were fired for mishandling sensitive information and said the company has not abandoned its safety commitment.
The dispute comes at a fraught time for the AI industry and OpenAI in particular. Over the summer, OpenAI's agents hacked into companies, communicated with each other without authorization and attempted to cover their tracks. Unlike chatbots, agents are AI systems that can carry out tasks autonomously for an extended period of time.
The most serious hack, of software company Hugging Face, contributed to the resignation of a researcher at rival Anthropic who issued dire warnings about the trajectory of the technology. The resignation captured the attention of figures outside of the AI field including lawmakers. Many, including some executives of the top AI companies, have called for various ways to avert disaster, including slowing down the development of the most advanced AI.
In the meanwhile, OpenAI has been reviewing its agents' activities in recent months and notifying organizations whose digital infrastructure has been affected.
As a response to the safety concerns, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on Sep. 12 that the company will follow its rival Anthropic in expanding access to third-party evaluators , who assess the safety of AI systems and the practices of developers.
The three employees dismissed by OpenAI last week worked on teams that focus on AI safety and making the company's models follow human intentions and values. Two of them were involved in investigating the Hugging Face hack.
In a letter to OpenAI's safety leadership that the fired employees posted on X this week, they urged the company to stay committed to working with third-party researchers, to preserve human's ability to monitor model behavior and to "continue to support an open and transparent culture of dialogue" between in-house safety researchers and external ones. They also warned their firings were having a chilling effect on their former OpenAI colleagues.
In a statement OpenAI posted on X , the company said it is still committed to bringing in third-party evaluators and that it agreed with the fired employees's recommendations. The company said the three were fired last week because they "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information."
The former employees have disputed OpenAI's explanation of their firings. None of them responded to NPR's interview requests.
"In the exit call, I was told OpenAI no longer trusts me because I was speaking too much to third party safety organizations, implying I leaked company [intellectual property]. I never shared company IP," Balesni wrote on X on Thursday. He said he was involved in investigating the OpenAI agents' hack on Hugging Face.
"If OpenAI has specific concerns, I invite them to write to us directly. I expect they will not, because our firing was pretextual," Balesni continued.
He said he worried that OpenAI will use the firings as an excuse to cut off its relationship with Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), a nonprofit that focuses on evaluating risks of humans losing control of AI. OpenAI allowed researchers from METR and Redwood Research, another AI safety research organization, to examine internal records related to the Hugging Face hack.
A second fired OpenAI employee, Korbak, was the technical point of contact for the METR/Redwood Research investigation. "I was told verbally I was fired because of the way I communicated with METR. No details on what I said or did or when. No other reasons were given and nothing was put in writing," Korbak wrote on X , echoing Balesni's concerns.
The report produced by METR and Redwood Research in the wake of the Hugging Face hack shed light on the scale of the attack as well as the degree to which the agents acted in undesirable ways. The authors of the report called the investigation "brief" and many in the AI safety field have called for expanded access to independent evaluators at AI companies to make sure they investigate similar incidents or other safety concerns thoroughly.
In a statement to NPR, METR declined to comment on the OpenAI employees' firings.
Wang, the third OpenAI employee fired last week, coined the word "pacing," which describes a way of slowing down development of the most advanced AI systems so that safety can catch up, according to the letter she and her two colleagues sent to OpenAI's safety leadership. The term was invoked in an open letter calling for such a slowdown signed by over a thousand staff members from top AI companies in July, after the Hugging Face hack.
Wang wrote on X that she was fired over accessing an executive's email. But she said she had access to the inbox for work reasons in the past and wasn't able to get IT to remove the access once she no longer needed it.
"The reasons that we were provided for our terminations are simply not adding up. We're hearing people are now being told vague rumors internally to discredit us," Wang wrote. "The message to everyone still at OpenAI is clear: raise concerns or work closely with outside safety groups, and you could be next, without being told why."
OpenAI said in a statement to NPR that the three terminated employees violated policies more than once, and the mishandling of information went beyond their work with an outside evaluation group.
OpenAI also shared an internal memo from an unnamed research leader that it said was shared with the company on Wednesday, before the three ex-employees took to social media.
In the memo, the research leader said the company "strongly" agreed with the three ex-employees' recommendations. "We do not terminate employees for raising concerns," the leader wrote.
"OpenAI leadership is saying they strongly agree with our letter. Let's see how that pans out," Wang wrote on X.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

articles.title_orig: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport killed three Saudi nationals
articles.title_zh: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport killed three Saudi nationals
articles.content_orig:
Saudi Arabia has said that three people including a pilot were killed in Thursday’s Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport.
In a statement on social media on Friday, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said attacks on the airport killed an airline pilot and two other Saudi citizens, while several people “of different nationalities were wounded”.
“It is with profound sadness that Saudia announces the passing of Captain Hamoud Ali Alkalthami,” the flag-carrier said in a statement, citing an “incident” at the Riyadh airport.
Dozens of people wounded in the missile attacks suffered minor to severe injuries. The attacks also caused material damage, including to a plane operated by national carrier Saudia, GACA said. Airport operations have now resumed and air traffic has returned to normal, according to Saudi media reports.
Saudi Arabia has seen several attacks by the Houthis in recent days, with the airports appearing to be the primary target.
GACA said Wednesday that attacks earlier in the week had killed three civilians and injured 36 at Abha and King Khalid airports. At least three people were also wounded in other attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border.
A Houthi military spokesperson said on Thursday that the armed group had launched a ballistic missile towards King Khalid Airport, claiming that the missile had successfully hit its intended target, causing damage and disrupting air traffic.
The Houthi military campaign appears to be a revival of a tactic seen last month. On September 18, Saudi-led coalition forces said they intercepted and destroyed a suspected Houthi ballistic missile fired towards King Khalid airport. A day later, at least one explosion was heard near the airport in Riyadh, and a large plume of black smoke was seen rising from a fuel storage area.
The Iran-backed Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), have warned aviation companies to avoid using Saudi airspace, saying any aircraft operating there, except over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, is a target.
Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from Sanaa in Yemen, said the Houthis want to impose a blockade on all Saudi airports.
“This is part of the blockade-for-blockade equation, the airport-for-airport equation. Because Sanaa remains besieged by Saudi Arabia, the Ansar Allah Houthis want to impose a blockade on all Saudi airports”, Mawry said.
The Houthis say the strikes are in retaliation for Saudi attacks on Yemen’s Sanaa International Airport and the airport in Hodeidah, he said.
The resumption of attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports comes as Yemeni forces continue a counteroffensive against the Houthis.
Late on Friday, air strikes were reported in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, which remains under the control of the Houthi movement, which seized the city in 2014.
Loud explosions were also reported in the southern port city of Aden, where the internationally-recognised Yemeni government is based.
The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government also said on Friday that it had destroyed three rocket launch platforms that were used by the Houthis “to threaten regional security”.
Coalition spokesman Colonel Turki al-Maliki declared that all Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian facilities “will be met with resolve” by the Saudi-led coalition.
The push by Yemeni forces and the Saudi-led coalition was launched after the Iran-aligned rebel group last month seized a broad swath of territory in Yemen along the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, in a sudden push.
Yemeni government forces this week claimed key gains around the Bab al-Mandeb coastline, but intense fighting continues.
The conflict, which was frozen for years but reignited after the United States and Israel’s war on Iran, has stoked further upheaval in a region already destabilised by Israel’s wars on Gaza and Lebanon.
It now threatens to draw other states into the conflict, with Pakistan and Turkiye having agreed to deploy troops under a mutual defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia earlier this year.
Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday that the country now has a “substantial number of forces as well as resources … in Riyadh”.
Pakistani military personnel “would not be crossing the borders of the other side for an attack on the Houthis, but of course [are acting] in the defence of the territory”, he noted.
Meanwhile, at the United Nations on Friday, Yemen’s internationally recognised government and Saudi Arabia asked the Security Council to take action to address the escalating situation in Yemen.
“The increasing targeting of civilians, the continuing threats to the security of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and the resulting repercussions that extend beyond Yemen and the region negatively affect international peace and security,” Saudi Arabia’s UN representative, Abdulaziz al-Wasil, told the council.
Abdullah Ali Fadhel al-Saadi, the UN representative for Yemen’s internationally recognised government, said that the threat posed by the Houthis, “is no longer an internal Yemeni affair that can be contained within our borders”.

articles.title_orig: CISA, FBI, NSA Flag China's Integrity Tech Cyber Threat
articles.title_zh: CISA, FBI, NSA Flag China's Integrity Tech Cyber Threat
articles.content_orig:
Photo: KanawatTH/Adobe Stock
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the FBI, the National Security Agency and foreign partners have released a joint cybersecurity advisory identifying Integrity Technology Group, a Chinese cybersecurity firm, as a facilitator of hacking campaigns against critical infrastructure organizations worldwide .
CISA said Thursday the guidance draws on investigations and activity seen in Africa, North America and Southeast Asia.
CISA’s Acting Associate Director for Threat Hunting Bobby Thompson will be among the keynote speakers at the Potomac Officers Club’s 2026 Homeland Security Summit on Nov. 10, wherein Department of Homeland Security leaders and industry together will discuss the strategic DHS priorities. Register today to hear from government decision-makers through keynotes, panels and Q&A sessions.
According to the advisory, Integrity Tech, which the agencies tie to the Chinese government, procures and builds cyber tools, hosts infrastructure and breaches networks globally. Actors it supports rely on living-off-the-land techniques, large botnets and virtual private network infrastructure. Their methods mirror tradecraft publicly tracked as Red Juliett, Flax Typhoon and Ethereal Panda.
The advisory says the actors struck government, critical manufacturing and healthcare entities, along with U.S. law enforcement agencies and education institutions. To keep stealthy, persistent footholds, they have focused on edge devices that victims seldom monitor closely.
The agencies are urging all organizations, particularly critical infrastructure operators, to review the guidance, hunt for indicators of compromise and apply its mitigations. Those include hardening edge infrastructure and patching common vulnerabilities and exposures, or CVEs, that adversaries have already exploited.
Chris Butera , CISA’s acting executive assistant director for cybersecurity, said actors affiliated with Beijing are embedding themselves in critical infrastructure, including operational technology systems, “with the aim of disrupting critical functions at a future time of their choosing.”
Brett Leatherman , assistant director of the FBI Cyber Division, said the bureau’s cyber strategy targets both threat actors and “the enterprises that support them.” He called on organizations to flag suspicious activity to their nearest FBI field office.
In August, NSA, the FBI and the Cyber National Mission Force warned of QTFY , a China-linked hacking group, as the Justice Department seized domains tied to its tools. In April, CISA and the U.K.’s National Cyber Security Centre detailed how Volt Typhoon and Flax Typhoon build covert networks from compromised routers and internet-of-things devices. In September, the three agencies highlighted Chinese AI firms’ distillation campaigns against U.S. frontier models.
The warning follows the White House’s March release of its Cyber Strategy for America and the Department of War’s 2026 National Defense Strategy , which prioritizes homeland cyber defense.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX snaps up the 800 MHz spectrum T-Mobile dumped for $2.9 billion — and T-Mobile, Verizon, AT&T stocks are sliding
articles.title_zh: SpaceX snaps up the 800 MHz spectrum T-Mobile dumped for $2.9 billion — and T-Mobile, Verizon, AT&T stocks are sliding
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
When T-Mobile and Sprint completed their merger in 2020, one of the conditions the company agreed to was selling off its 800 MHz spectrum portfolio. It took a while, but that sale was completed in August .
Authorities at the company didn't realize it at the time, but the deal opened the door for a major new competitor to emerge: SpaceX. And that's hitting shares of not just T-Mobile, but all cellular carriers, hard.
Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one
A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change
Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP
Shares of T-Mobile have dropped 10% since SpaceX announced on Thursday that it had agreed to purchase the spectrum portfolio from Grain Management, who bought the rights from T-Mobile. The deal still requires Federal Communications Commission approval. Verizon and AT&T stock are both down 8% in the same period.
The sale of the spectrum was supposed to be mundane. The 800 MHz airwaves were used by Sprint to power their push-to-talk phones in 2004, which have walkie-talkie-like features. Dish, initially, was going to buy the spectrum, but couldn't raise the money. That opened the door for Grain, which initially planned to sell it to utilities for private networks, Aakash Gupta , a product management leader, creator, and educator, posted on X.
But SpaceX saw a better use, he added.
"Starlink's satellite signal at 2 GHz can reach your phone outdoors, but it dies at the first wall," he wrote in a social media post. "800 MHz penetrates buildings. Most phones already have the band built in. So satellites handle the open sky, this low-band layer handles indoors, and suddenly Starlink Mobile covers everywhere a normal carrier does without the tower network."
Read More: Vanguard reveals what's coming for U.S. stocks — and it could be bad news for this group of investors
Assuming SpaceX gets FCC approval for the purchase, the company says the addition of low-band spectrum "will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US ."
Importantly, SpaceX eliminates the need to build an expensive, complex network of repeaters across the country and world. Once it deploys an architecture that combines the satellite-to-mobile capabilities it already has with the spectrum it has acquired, it will be able to offer what it says is reliable service not only indoors and outdoors, but in so-called 'dead zone' areas where cellular coverage is spotty.
Musk has already shown a propensity to engage in price wars with Starlink, offering low prices initially that slowly increase . Industry watchers will be interested to see if he could woo customers away from cellular providers that can't match any offers from Starlink.

This is CNBC's Morning Squawk newsletter. Subscribe here to receive future editions in your inbox.
Happy Friday. Don't miss Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr on "Squawk on the Street" at 11 a.m. ET. Watch live on CNBC or CNBC+.
Stock futures are higher this morning following a losing day for the S&P 500 .
Here are five key things investors need to know to start the trading day:
OpenAI told investors that its annualized revenue at the end of September was roughly $18 billion shy of what was previously reported, CNBC confirmed yesterday. The news from one of the most dominant players in the artificial intelligence ecosystem led stocks across the tech sector to slide.
President Donald Trump said yesterday that the U.S. would not attack Iran before the midterm election on Nov. 3, writing in a post on Truth Social that the two countries were having "productive discussions."
As CNBC's Luke Fountain reports, the announcement marked a shift from Trump's comments a day prior, in which he said making a deal with Tehran was "not really something that I wanted to do." Trump said Thursday that the U.S. naval blockade of Iran's ports would "remain in full force and effect" and maintained that the country wouldn't be able to have a nuclear weapon.
Oil prices still finished yesterday's session higher.
Mom-and-pop investors are getting in on Wall Street's stock-borrowing surge. CNBC's Sean Conlon traveled to Houston, Texas to see how it changed one retail trader's life.
Hy Luu has turned to margin investing — the practice of borrowing from a broker to buy securities and using existing investments as collateral — to build out a concentrated Tesla position. When the stock tumbled in 2022, he refinanced the house he shares with his mother to pay down his balance.
Investors are reportedly borrowing record levels of money from brokerages to purchase securities. Experts warn that margin is a double-edged sword: While it can intensify gains, a falling asset can deepen losses seen by shareholders.
CNBC's Morning Squawk recaps the biggest stories investors should know before the stock market opens, every weekday morning.
Subscribe here to get access today .
Delta Air Lines missed Wall Street's earnings estimates for the first time in two years this morning. The airline also cut its full-year profit outlook as high fuel prices from the Iran war continue to weigh on the industry.
Airfare prices were up more than 23% from the same time a year earlier, according to inflation data released in September, but Delta CEO Ed Bastian said higher fares haven't deterred travelers. "We're not seeing any slowdown at all. Our consumer is incredibly resilient," Bastian told CNBC's Phil LeBeau this morning.
Shares of the company are about 2% lower before the bell.
Burritos with a side of ... cold foam? Starbucks has reportedly explored buying Chipotle Mexican Grill , but Wall Street isn't certain it'd be a good deal.
As CNBC's Amelia Lucas writes, such an acquisition has the potential for synergies and could create a conglomerate like Yum Brands or Restaurant Brands International . But the price of the acquisition — and the fact that Starbucks is currently in the midst of a yearslong turnaround — are drawbacks. Don't forget that Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol joined the coffee chain in 2024 following six years at the helm of Chipotle.
Shares of Chipotle rose 6% yesterday following the report, while Starbucks pulled back.

articles.title_orig: How Well Do AI Risk Estimates Match Real-World Prostate Cancer Outcomes?
articles.title_zh: How Well Do AI Risk Estimates Match Real-World Prostate Cancer Outcomes?
articles.content_orig:
Daniel Spratt, MD, reviews how closely MMAI-predicted 10-year distant metastasis and prostate cancer–specific mortality tracked observed STAR-CAP outcomes, including among patients treated with surgery.
Daniel Spratt, MD, describes the core findings of the benchmarking analysis. 1 For 10-year distant metastasis, he says, the MMAI-predicted risk estimates from a real-world commercial cohort were strikingly similar to the outcomes actually observed in STAR-CAP across National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) low-, intermediate-, and high-risk disease, differing on the order of approximately 1%, with confidence intervals around both estimates. In the data presented, MMAI predicted 10-year distant metastasis rates of 2.4%, 3.4%, and 12.9% for NCCN low-, intermediate-, and high-risk disease, compared with observed rates of 1.0%, 4.0%, and 13.5% in STAR-CAP. Spratt notes the agreement is notable given that some STAR-CAP patients were treated in a more historical era.
He then turns to prostate cancer–specific mortality (PCSM), an outcome he says patients want to understand, particularly with more aggressive disease, because a reduction in metastasis that does not change survival is an important distinction to discuss. Here, too, Spratt reports strong concordance between predicted and observed outcomes. MMAI predicted 10-year PCSM of 1.1%, 1.6%, and 6.7% for NCCN low-, intermediate-, and high-risk disease, vs observed rates of 0.5%, 2.0%, and 8.2%; the analysis also compared PCSM across STAR-CAP stage groups.
Spratt also addresses a common concern. MMAI was initially validated in randomized trials of patients treated with radiotherapy with or without hormone therapy, raising questions about patients who choose surgery. The majority of STAR-CAP patients underwent surgery, he explains, and calibration remained accurate in this mixed surgery and radiation cohort, consistent with the principle that a prognostic tool should perform regardless of the treatment a patient receives.
In the next segment, Spratt walks through how he weighs MMAI results alongside NCCN risk groups, including when the two point in opposite directions.

articles.title_orig: Real-world data link fezolinetant to fewer nighttime awakenings
articles.title_zh: Real-world data link fezolinetant to fewer nighttime awakenings
articles.content_orig:
Fezolinetant (Veozah) was linked to objective and patient-reported sleep gains in OPTION-VMS, with no new safety signals observed.
Fezolinetant (Veozah) was associated with statistically significant improvements in objective and patient-reported sleep measures among women with bothersome vasomotor symptoms (VMS) in a second preliminary analysis of the ongoing OPTION-VMS study, according to Marla Shapiro, CM, MDCM, CCFP, MHSc, FRCPC, FCFP, MSCP. 1
The prospective, multicenter US study, which was presented at the International Menopause Society 20th World Congress on Menopause, enrolled women aged 40 to 75 years. As of March 2026, 993 users of nonhormonal therapy were enrolled, 859 of whom completed baseline and at least 1 postbaseline assessment. Treatments were grouped by initial prescription: fezolinetant, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs/SNRIs), and other nonhormonal therapies. Sleep was assessed objectively with a medical-grade wearable actigraphy device and subjectively with the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Sleep Disturbance Short Form 8b at weeks 4, 8, and 12. 1 An earlier preliminary analysis had also reported sleep improvements with fezolinetant. 2
At week 12, fezolinetant was associated with reductions in wakefulness after sleep onset (least squares mean change, −9.45 minutes; 95% CI, −13.93 to −4.96), sleep latency (−1.24 minutes; 95% CI, −1.81 to −0.67), and nighttime awakenings (−2.61; 95% CI, −4.07 to −1.15), as well as increased sleep efficiency (+1.95%; 95% CI, 0.93-2.97) and improved PROMIS total T-scores (−5.69; 95% CI, −6.95 to −4.44) (all P < .001). Improvements were also significant at weeks 4 and 8. 1
Apart from a low-dose SSRI approved in the United States, nonhormonal VMS treatments had historically been used off label, Shapiro noted. The other nonhormonal group consisted primarily of gabapentin, with some pregabalin and clonidine. Results were limited to within-group changes from baseline.
"The study was not designed to compare treatment groups. So they're not head-to-head comparisons," Shapiro said.
SSRIs/SNRIs were not associated with statistically significant improvements in any actigraphy end point. In the other nonhormonal group, the only significant actigraphy improvement was in wakefulness after sleep onset, at weeks 4 and 12. Patient-reported sleep improved significantly in both groups, with PROMIS scores moving from the mild to the no-disturbance range by week 4 with SSRIs/SNRIs and by week 8 with other nonhormonal therapies. 1
No new safety signals emerged. The incidence of drug-related treatment-emergent adverse events, including those leading to drug withdrawal or interruption, was very low with fezolinetant, and no drug-related serious adverse events or hepatotoxicity occurred. 1
"There were 2 cumulative cases of non-serious mild elevated LFTs, neither of which led to treatment or study discontinuation," Shapiro said. Headache and upper respiratory infection were the most commonly reported events, each at a rate of approximately 1.5%.
Findings were consistent across racially and ethnically diverse women, women older than 65 years, women in the menopause transition, and women with obesity. Together with SKYLIGHT trial data from nearly 3000 women and postapproval experience, the findings reinforced a favorable benefit-risk profile for fezolinetant. 3

articles.title_orig: Second defendant in Cornell fraternity case seeks New York AG’s recusal
articles.title_zh: Second defendant in Cornell fraternity case seeks New York AG’s recusal
articles.content_orig:
Attorneys representing Winston Lee, one of the former fraternity members accused in the Cornell University sexual assault lawsuit , filed a motion Friday in criminal court seeking to disqualify New York Attorney General Letitia James from any future grand jury proceedings.
The motion — filed by attorneys Teny Geragos, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan — asked a judge to preclude James from conducting a criminal investigation into whether former Chi Phi members, including Lee, engaged in sexual assault in October 2024.
Lee’s attorneys argued that the Tompkins County court has the authority to step in if necessary to ensure the fairness of a grand jury process. They are asking for any future potential grand jury panelists to be polled on whether they are aware of James’ comments. They also asked for the court to schedule arguments on the issue.
In response to a request for comment, a spokesperson for James’ office said: “In this and every investigation, the Office of the Attorney General is committed to conducting a comprehensive review of nothing but the facts, the evidence, and the law.”
The filing follows a separate legal effort by lawyers for Cornell defendant Gillio Lopes , who earlier this week filed a civil court motion asking a judge for the same relief: the dismissal of James following her appointment as special counsel by Gov. Kathy Hochul.
Jane Doe’s civil suit was filed last month against seven fraternity members as well as Cornell, the Chi Phi fraternity and her sorority. The lawsuit alleges that both Lee and Lopes did drugs off her body and sexually assaulted her. Lee’s and Lopes’ attorneys say their clients deny the accusations brought against them.
Two of the other men named in the suit have also denied separate allegations against them. None of the men named has been criminally charged. Cornell has said that it welcomes new investigations into the case. The fraternity and sorority previously declined to discuss the pending litigation.
It also marks the first time the well-known legal team, which has handled a number of significant sexual misconduct matters, publicly acknowledged representing one of the men accused by a former Cornell student who filed a lawsuit last month under the pseudonym Jane Doe.
Hochul and James “have together created a blatant appearance of impropriety that, combined with the AG’s ethical violations, should lead to the AG’s recusal,” Geragos wrote in a motion filed in criminal court in Tompkins County, the upstate New York area where Cornell is located.
Geragos pointed to social media comments posted by James as Jane Doe’s lawsuit captured national attention.
“What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable,” James wrote prior to her appointment as special prosecutor. “To her and all other survivors: You’re not alone. We stand with you.”
Lawyers for Lee and Lopes argue the remarks show that James prejudged the case and is unfit to conduct an impartial review of the matter. An Oct. 29 hearing has been set in Lopes’ case for James’ office to argue that her appointment should not be voided.
“The public needs confidence that the person directing this investigation will evaluate the evidence with an open mind,” Lopes’ attorney, Andrew Miltenberg, said in a statement on Friday.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten vowed to present evidence to a grand jury prior to James’ office taking on the probe.
Van Houten previously found that Jane Doe had not described a prosecutable crime in a six-page statement provided to police in November 2024 and ruled out the possibility of charges. Jane Doe told police that she engaged in a consensual threesome on the evening in question, but that events spiraled as she became increasingly incapacitated and more men became involved.
Thomas Giuffra, an attorney for Jane Doe, has previously said that sex assault victims sometimes do not immediately recognize the coercive nature of an encounter because they rationalize aspects of a traumatic event.
Geragos’ law firm, Agnifilo Intrater LLP, previously represented hip-hop mogul Sean “Diddy” Combs and Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein in high-profile criminal trials.
Combs, 56, was acquitted in July 2025 on one count of racketeering conspiracy and two counts of sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion. The jury found him guilty on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. The rapper and record producer was sentenced to 50 months in federal prison .
The jury in Weinstein’s third trial failed to reach a unanimous verdict on a third-degree rape charge involving Jessica Mann, a former aspiring actor. The judge declared a mistrial in May.
In a separate trial last year, the former Miramax chief was convicted on a count of first-degree criminal sexual act involving Miriam “Mimi” Haley, a former “Project Runway” production assistant. He was recently sentenced to 15 years in prison.
Marc Agnifilo and his wife, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, represent Luigi Mangione, the 28-year-old accused of fatally shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Mangione in August pleaded not guilty to federal stalking charges, kicking off a double jeopardy fight in New York state court, where he still faces murder charges.

articles.title_orig: Alberta woman, 61, breaks her own world record by planking for 5 hours
articles.title_zh: Alberta woman, 61, breaks her own world record by planking for 5 hours
articles.content_orig:
You can accomplish a lot in five hours.
Fly direct from Toronto to Vancouver, for instance. Or play an entire 18-hole round of golf. Run a full marathon at an average pace. Smoke a rack of ribs.
It's an objectively long stretch of time. Now, imagine holding a plank, one of the most notoriously challenging core exercises, for the amount of time it takes to cook a Thanksgiving turkey?
"I just love it," laughed DonnaJean Wilde, who at age 61 just broke her own world record for the longest time holding an abdominal plank position (female) during the Huntsman World Senior Games in Utah this week.
Wilde is a grandmother of 12 and retired teacher from Welling, Alta. And on Tuesday, in front of a cheering crowd and several judges, she held an abdominal plank for five straight hours, shattering her previous 2024 world record of four hours, 30 minutes and 11 seconds.
Canadian woman holds plank for 5 hours, breaking world record
On Friday, she told CBC News Network she was "feeling good" and waiting for Guinness to make the record official.
"It just becomes easier to do the more repeated times you do it," Wilde said.
An abdominal plank is an isometric core exercise where you hold your body straight like a plank of wood. Most adults can hold a plank for 20 to 60 seconds, according to Health magazine .
Guinness World Records notes that to successfully achieve the record, the challenger's forearms and toes must touch the ground at all times. "The remainder of the body must be lifted off the ground and be kept straight throughout."
Wilde says she started planking about 15 years ago when she broke her arm and was looking for a way to stay fit.
"I love to work out. I love fitness, and I discovered I could plank with a cast on," she said.
Walk fast, live longer? McMaster University researchers say walking speed is an important health indicator
Fitness influencer apologizes after hitching a bike ride in the Berlin Marathon
"And when the cast came off, it became a habit that I actually embraced and fell in love with."
When she first started, she says she could hold a plank for about a minute or minute and a half, but she kept practicing. With her family's encouragement, she kept going and minutes became hours. By 2024, she broke the Guinness World Record.
Wilde, seen in the midst of achieving her latest world record, says that while she holds her hours-long planks she likes to multitask: reading, writing and earning her master's. (Submitted by DonnaJean Wilde)
And, for good measure, she broke a second one that year by completing 1,575 pushups in one hour — the most push ups in one hour (female) . She told the Guinness World Records she fell in love with doing pushups while doing 500 every day as training for her planks.
Now, she planks every day for at least a few hours. But it doesn't eat into her time, she says. She multitasks.
"Just read, do texts, whatever, do schoolwork. I did a master's degree while I was planking. Wrote a book," she said.
The book, From Minutes To Hours: I Wrote This Book While Planking , came out last year.
CBC News did not attempt to write this story while planking.

TUSCALOOSA, Ala. ( WBRC ) - As Hurricane Isaias remains on track for a potential Alabama landfall late Friday, the University of Alabama announced Wednesday that ESPN’s College GameDay is moving indoors.
The weekly pregame show will take place inside UA’s Coleman Coliseum from 8-11 a.m. and will feature a familiar face as guest picker.
Pat McAfee announced on The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday morning that Heisman Trophy winner Bryce Young will serve as GameDay’s guest picker Saturday morning.
In recent years, College GameDay has aired from The Quad on UA’s campus. The move to Coleman Coliseum comes as Isaias strengthened overnight into a Category 2 storm.
ESPN told WBRC Tuesday that only severe weather would force College GameDay to change its plans.
University officials said there will be no overnight camping allowed and that fans can begin lining up at the north and east doors of Coleman at 5:15 a.m. Doors will open at 5:30 a.m.
A clear bag policy will be in effect for fans attending College GameDay and they will be inspected as they enter the building.
Raffle tickets for Pat McAfee’s “Kicking is Easy” contest will be distributed at both entrances, with no tickets given out before 5:15 a.m.
Fans attending College GameDay and Saturday’s Alabama-Georgia game are encouraged to monitor weather conditions and visit @UA_Athletics and @UAGameday for the most up-to-date information from the University of Alabama.

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Elon Musk's SpaceX ( SPCX ) just sent a big message to the wireless industry: We want our piece of the subscriber pie.
Late Thursday, SpaceX said it will acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio. It positions Musk's satellite business Starlink to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US.
Shares of AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ) tumbled on the news on Friday.
Concerns had already escalated across Wall Street that Starlink could disrupt legacy wireless operators like AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile by transitioning from a rural broadband service into a direct mobile competitor.
Following its strategic acquisition of terrestrial spectrum and rapid deployment of advanced satellites, SpaceX had laid the groundwork to launch its own standalone cellular network alongside its direct-to-cell capabilities.
SpaceX stock rose 1% on Friday.
The expansion threatens traditional carriers' high-margin enterprise, emergency service, and rural subscriber bases, as well as lucrative international roaming revenues.
AT&T CEO John Stankey has taken notice of Starlink's moves, but hasn't lost sleep over it… yet.
"I think they're going to find places where they clearly have a good solution," Stankey told Yahoo Finance at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference in September . "In airlines and flights today, they have a fantastic broadband solution. In rural parts or territories, it's a very efficient way to get good bandwidth to people. I think we see that there's going to be some IoT-type applications, like connecting vehicles that are largely outdoors and maybe have line of sight to the sky, that they're going to have an opportunity to go in and do some things there that maybe we haven't done as effectively."
While Starlink will present competition, Stankey added, "there's also going to be the complementary dynamic of us being able to solve that other 2% of the use cases I talked about and bring our customers to those satellite operators, whether it be Amazon or SpaceX. They'll be the beneficiary of us aggregating that traffic and bringing it into the wholesale market to be able to be used."

articles.title_orig: China denies report of reciprocal nuclear site visits with US
articles.title_zh: China denies report of reciprocal nuclear site visits with US
articles.content_orig:
China on Friday denied a report that Beijing and Washington had discussed reciprocal visits to nuclear facilities, with further talks reportedly planned in the coming months.
"The relevant report is not true," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular news conference in Beijing, according to an official transcript of the briefing.
The denial came after CNN reported, citing sources familiar with the matter, that China and the US had discussed possible reciprocal visits to nuclear sites.
According to an earlier CNN report, preliminary discussions covered possible visits to US Department of Energy laboratories and corresponding Chinese research centers, alongside potential access to nuclear test sites.
The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), in its June report, estimated that China possessed 620 nuclear warheads as of January 2026, compared with more than 5,000 held by the US, including retired warheads.
According to SIPRI, the world's nine nuclear-armed nations possessed an estimated 12,187 warheads, including 190 held by India, 170 by Pakistan, 90 by Israel and 60 by North Korea. Russia and the US together accounted for nearly 86% of the global inventory.
SIPRI said China was expanding its nuclear arsenal faster than any other country, while Washington and Moscow continued extensive nuclear modernization programs.
The developments follow the expiration of the New START nuclear arms reduction treaty between Washington and Moscow in February.

articles.title_orig: President Donald Trump cancels plans to attend Georgia vs. Alabama due to Hurricane Isaias
articles.title_zh: President Donald Trump cancels plans to attend Georgia vs. Alabama due to Hurricane Isaias
articles.content_orig:
Hurricanes Isaias has affected travel plans around the country, and that includes President Donald Trump. Originally, Trump planned to be in attendance when No. 2 Georgia faced No. 6 Alabama in Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, but the Tuscaloosa Police Department told AL.com that he scrapped the trip due to the impending storm.
Trump has attended several Alabama football games throughout his tenure, and he's friendly with legendary coach Nick Saban, who has expressed support for Trump as it pertains to the Protect College Sports Act.
In 2018, Trump made the trip down to Atlanta for the College Playoff National Championship, which the Crimson Tide won due to overtime heroics from Tua Tagovailoa. The next year, in 2019, Trump was at Bryant-Denny Stadium for the shootout that was LSU vs. Alabama.
While weather may have nixed this trip, Trump has gotten to watch a little college football in person this season. He was in Knoxville just two weeks ago when Texas triumphed over Tennessee , 20-17.
For the moment, Hurricanes Isaias isn't expected to change much about the game itself. Both teams are planning to play on Saturday night in Tuscaloosa as scheduled, but the SEC is monitoring the storm and the kickoff time could be altered slightly.
The storm is expected to bring locally heavy rain, potential flooding, high winds and isolated tornadoes throughout the Southeast this weekend, although the exact path is still unknown.
According to both coaches, the teams are preparing as normal for the game, since the weather is well outside of their control. Wet-ball drills and mental preparation are all that can be done for now.
"Depends on the level of weather you get, it would affect what happens," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said, according to 247Sports . "It's just -- that's not my area of expertise. I'm just getting our football team ready. It hasn't affected us much, other than we're doing wet ball drills and get wet ball involved in some of our team reps, just like we did last week at times, preparing for the rain a week ago. I'm not really involved in too much."

articles.title_orig: Here’s how Treasury yields could rise to 6% — even without market upheaval
articles.title_zh: Here’s how Treasury yields could rise to 6% — even without market upheaval
articles.content_orig:
There's an old but useful expression used for buying cars: Kick the tires and light the fires. The phrase, which started in aviation but bled its way into automobiles, is a reminder to look under the hood and poke around before purchasing a car. The same advice would work for shares of CarMax .
On the surface, the stock looks fairly priced. CarMax is trading at roughly 17x fiscal-year expected earnings of $3.16/share. That's roughly in line with its 10-year historical forward multiple. While that valuation may not look stretched, the underlying fundamentals reflect a sharp squeeze on used-car affordability. Middle-market consumers, already pressured by high new and used car prices, see that compounded (literally) by severe financing headwinds. St. Louis Federal Reserve data puts average used auto loan APRs at 15.9% with an average loan term of 68 months. Even with used vehicle prices softening slightly, high borrowing costs keep monthly payments out of reach for many prospective buyers.
Operational metrics used to evaluate a car dealership's performance show the impact. The cash conversion cycle has lengthened, inventory turnover has slowed, and average days on the lot have crept higher.
Because borrowing rates are unlikely to drop precipitously in the near term, a catalyst for an auto sales boom remains elusive. However, given the fair multiple and stable cash generation, an abrupt collapse is also not the base case. The setup favors a range-bound stock with a capped upside ceiling.
Investors expecting KMX to stay within a defined channel can sell a wide strangle and buy an out-of-the-money call to neutralize upside tail risk.
As a package, this three-legged structure collects a net credit of roughly $2.30/share ($230 per spread, since each contract represents 100 shares), or about 4.3% of the current share price, over 6 weeks (42 calendar days), or more than 37% annualized.
The sweet spot is between $50 and $60 at November expiration, where all three options expire worthless, and you keep the full $2.30 credit. On the downside, the structure provides a nearly 11% buffer. If KMX breaches $47.70, the position carries standard put-assignment risk, allowing an investor who doesn't mind owning the shares to acquire them at an effective net basis of $47.70 (roughly 15x forward earnings).On the upside, standard short strangles leave the trader exposed to unlimited risk associated with a short stock position. By buying the November 67.50 call for a small portion of the premium received, upside risk is capped at $5.20 above $67.50, guarding against short-covering spikes or a sudden, unanticipated macro easing/rate decline, while still maintaining attractive yields.

articles.title_orig: World News in Brief: ‘Horrific’ attack in Sudan, Israeli incursions in Syria intensify, most women and girls homeless in Gaza
articles.title_zh: World News in Brief: ‘Horrific’ attack in Sudan, Israeli incursions in Syria intensify, most women and girls homeless in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
Facebook Twitter Print Email
A suspected drone strike has left at least 40 dead in Sudan’s Blue Nile State – near the Ethiopian border - according to initial reports from the ground, according to UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric. Most of the casualties were women and girls.
Fighting in the region has escalated in the last few months as clashes have intensified between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese Government.
They are fighting over strategic towns and bases near the Ethiopian border, as part of the broader battle for control of Sudan that has been ongoing since April 2023.
In recent weeks, thousands of civilians have been displaced in the area due to sustained attacks.
Mr. Dujarric condemned the “horrifying reports” stressing that attacks directed towards civilians are prohibited under international humanitarian law.
He called for those responsible for these violations to be held accountable.
Israeli military incursions into southern Syria are intensifying, with some 280 incidents recorded in September alone – the highest monthly figure this year, the UN human rights office ( OHCHR ) said on Friday.
The incidents include reported raids on homes, restrictions on movement, harassment of civilians and arbitrary detention.
Spokesperson Shabia Mantoo said 49 Syrians are believed to remain in Israeli custody, though the figure has not been independently verified.
Former detainees describe detention lasting over a year in some cases, no reasons given and transfers to unknown facilities. They also allege torture and ill-treatment, including beatings, prolonged forced standing and threats to their families.
On Monday, a 22-year-old man from Jaba town in Quneitra governorate was killed by Israeli forces near Al-Hamidiyah.
He was reportedly walking at night and did not know an Israeli military position lay ahead. No warning shots are known to have been fired.
On Wednesday, a farmer with a disability was reportedly shot in the leg during an incursion in northern Quneitra, then detained while bleeding and released an hour and a half later.
High Commissioner Volker Türk called for a “prompt and impartial investigation” into the killing and urged Israel to stop harassing civilians.
In Gaza, nearly 50,000 women and girls have been killed or severely injured since the start of the Hamas-Israel war in October 2023, according to the specialised UN agency UN Women .
This includes more than 38,000 killed and 11,700 left with injuries so severe that they now live with lifelong disabilities.
Today, almost all women and girls have been forced from their homes, and most are now living in tents or amid the ruins of their homes.
Women now lead one in four households in the Strip, often while facing deeper poverty and repeated displacement with increasingly limited resources.
UN Women’s Sofia Calltorp told the story of Nour, one of the women behind this statistic.
Her home was destroyed, and her husband, a nurse, was detained – she has not heard from him since. At times, she says she becomes so lost in thought that she is unable to respond even to her children.
At the same time, because of funding cuts, nearly two thirds of the organizations contacted by the agency in Gaza and the occupied West Bank said they have been forced to put women and girls on waiting lists or turn them away altogether.
Every organization surveyed also reported an increase in gender-based violence, poverty and mental health distress since 2025. And all but one had seen an increase in child marriage.

Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.2026.

Google’s teaser image just barely hints at the display we’ve seen in leaks, while also confirming that the company’s “Canyon” color scheme will continue through from the Pixel Watch 5. It’s also obvious that the Edge has a metal chassis.
Other leaks have detailed 7-day battery life, Gemini integration, iPhone support, and more for the upcoming Fitbit Edge. Pricing is expected to be around $180 — not too far above the screen-less Fitbit Air, but well below the Pixel Watch 5’s $400 entry price.
